findings.title: Settings discrepancies have no resolution flow
findings.why_it_matters: A user can reach a blocked setup state without any defined way to make the valuation actionable, so planning must guess how source conflicts are resolved and which value becomes authoritative. A field-level confirmation and correction flow would turn the stated discrepancy warning into a complete path with a clear ready state.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a setup flow that lists each material discrepancy, lets the user confirm or correct the authoritative value and source, and shows when all ceiling-blocking fields are resolved.
evidence: Unresolved material settings prevent actionable ceilings.
findings.disposition: Returned to caller for later planning; not treated as accepted user choice.

findings.title: Live controls lack accessibility requirements
findings.section: Proposed personalized experience: Completed sales and nominations
findings.why_it_matters: Users who rely on a keyboard or assistive technology may be unable to enter time-sensitive sales, update prices, correct mistakes, or detect when an actionable quote changes. Explicit keyboard operation, focus behavior, and announced status updates give planning the accessibility contract needed for the live workflow.
findings.suggested_fix: Require keyboard operation for sale entry, nominee and price updates, undo, and correction; preserve predictable focus after each action; and announce reconciliation, suppression, error, and refreshed-quote status to assistive technology.
evidence: After a completed sale: record player, winning team, and cost.
When a player is nominated: select the player and enter current price.
Undo/correction rebuilds state from the ledger.
findings.disposition: Returned unapplied in non-interactive mode; no user question during overnight investigation.

synthesis.rationale: Both findings remain at confidence 75. The settings-resolution proposal is a genuine UX choice. The accessibility proposal remains a concrete grouped-confirmation item. Neither qualifies for unattended application.
